newsitem.title: USA: Occidental says losses from Cano minimal.
newsitem.headline: Occidental says losses from Cano minimal.

text.p: The financial impact on Occidental Corp of lost production from the Cano Limon field in Colombia, which has been shut-in since after a rebel bomb attack, is minimal, according to a company spokesman.
"The financial impact on Occidental is not material," said Occidental spokesman Lawrence Meriage, who estimated that the cost of lost production was about $100,000 a day while the field was shut.

Meriage said Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol has estimated that lost production is valued at $3.3. million a day. But Occidental, though operator of the field, has only an 18 percent share in the field's production, while other partners Shell and Ecopetrol own the rest.
The spokesman said the bombed pipeline, which has shut in production since last Monday, is still expected to be fixed by this weekend.
"It's the rainy season there and that might affect things, but we expect it to be back up, if all goes according to plan, by the weekend," Meriage said.
The field was producing at a rate of about 175,000 barrels per day before the latest attack.
